Known Foundry named Live creation for the Identity Digital registry. This Node.js package is separate from the protocol core; `@dnsid-ai/sdk` does not import or re-export it.

## Contract and server gate

Implements compliance design commit `89600ed`. No deployed server revision has passed the required SR-1 through SR-7 acceptance checks. The package is marked `private: true`, so the release workflow skips packing and publishing it. Remove that flag only after server acceptance, and record the accepted server revision with the SDK release. Initial-create acceptance must include server refusal of terminal-name replacement for every key; without local state, the SDK cannot detect a replacement. There is no sandbox fallback, ordinary-registration fallback, or capability probe beyond authenticated onboarding.

`create(name, options?)` loads environment configuration when `options.config` is absent. Explicit merged configuration does not re-read the environment. `FoundryConfig` is a plain data type owned and exported by the config loader (`@dnsid-ai/sdk/node`), not by Foundry. Registry credentials are separate from configuration. Applications can inject the registry, key provider, public DNS/HTTPS dependencies, log registry, and store through the same options.

Names are exact Unicode strings, not domains: no trimming, case changes, or Unicode normalization. The server allocates the domain. Create persists registration facts but does not wait for public ACTIVE. A challenge-free replay without a domain saves the ID and status and returns a resumable error. Until both ID and domain are saved, the next `create()` replays the same frozen request and registration key. It does not search the agent list.

`active({signal?, timeoutMs?})` finishes proof and shared managed issuance, then verifies fresh public DNS, HTTPS, current keys, status, and lifecycle-log evidence. Initial setup does not scan lifecycle history before preparation. Saved accepted issuance is verified without resubmission. An issuance rejection (`IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`, `TLOG_PREPARATION_MISMATCH`, or `TLOG_INVALID_ENTRY`) triggers lifecycle recovery; empty history or a missing ISSUANCE returns a resumable error rather than authorizing new preparation. Registry READY does not imply protocol ACTIVE. Default deadlines are 30 seconds for `create()` and 10 minutes for `active()`; callers can override either with `timeoutMs`. Polling and transient retries start at 1 second, double to a 15-second cap, and stay within the call's deadline. Cancellation retains progress and never cancels the server identity. Non-cancellable provider calls are checked before and after; the provider must bound its own calls.

`sign(bytes)` adds no signature format. It shares its pause controller with profile helpers built from `identityManager()`. Until step 5 saves publication configuration, `identityManager()` throws `SigningPaused` and creates nothing. Later calls return one normally constructed manager. Signing remains paused until public readiness succeeds. Reopening a completed operation with saved state checks the saved current public-key binding without DNS/log calls; `active()` refreshes it. Terminal or key-binding failures pause signing. A deadline or cancellation during refresh leaves an already enabled signer enabled. Direct access to the underlying provider is outside this guard. After rotation, a replica without saved state derives a new registration key from its current key and receives `KEY_MISMATCH`; it does not attempt to resolve that server-gated case.

## Storage and recovery

`FileFoundryStore` defaults to `~/.dnsid/foundry/`. State paths digest the registry URL, organization ID, and exact name. `proof-pending` lasts until its outcome is saved; then `identity-known` covers ISSUANCE preparation and submission until acceptance. Files are owner-only, atomically renamed, and fsynced. Each call holds an in-process/cross-process lock, reloads state, and releases the lock only after writes finish. Locks do not expire while their owning process lives; an observed dead process can be reclaimed. PID reuse conservatively leaves the operation busy until that process exits. The lock is safe on one host and in one PID namespace only. Do not share the directory across hosts or containers: reclaim checks the local PID and can remove a lock held elsewhere. Use a local filesystem with atomic directory rename and file/directory fsync. Inject a store with equivalent locking and durability for shared storage.

Export and import use version-1 UTF-8 JCS recovery documents. Duplicate members, invalid Unicode, unsupported phases/versions, conflicting input, and invalid completed-byte hashes are rejected. Unknown members survive rewrites. Recovery files contain public bindings and provider references, never private keys or registry credentials. Save a backup of recovery files **and** independently recoverable provider keys. Back up the whole directory, including historical identity snapshots. Container-local storage is lost when its volume is removed. An ephemeral injected checkpoint store does not supply restart-persistent log rollback protection; inject a log registry with a durable checkpoint store when required.

The local file key provider does not provision keys on this facade's behalf. An empty injected provider can implement `ensureSigningKey({signal})`; key provisioning and replica convergence remain the provider's responsibility. An established binding never triggers provisioning to repair a missing or different key.

Proof-expiry rejection recovery is deferred until the server defines its error code. CLI, hosted cross-SDK scenarios, key-provider provisioning internals, rotation, and retirement/revocation workflows are not implemented here. Same-name replacement is disabled and returns a terminal error.

<a id="stacktracelimit"></a>

##### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:67

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

###### Inherited from

```ts
Error.stackTraceLimit
```

#### Methods

<a id="capturestacktrace"></a>

##### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:51

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

###### Parameters

###### targetObject

`object`

###### constructorOpt?

`Function`

###### Returns

`void`

#### Methods

<a id="capturestacktrace-1"></a>

##### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:51

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

###### Parameters

###### targetObject

`object`

###### constructorOpt?

`Function`

###### Returns

`void`

<a id="stacktracelimit-2"></a>

##### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:67

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

###### Inherited from

[`FoundryError`](#foundryerror).[`stackTraceLimit`](#stacktracelimit)
